basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 4.' and it opens 'Vers. 4. Javan filii, Elisa, a quo Elisei, id est, Graeci qui et Hellades appellantur.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 4. Javan filii, Elisa, a quo Elisei, id est, Graeci qui et Hellades appellantur. Tharsis Cilices quorum civitas est Tharsus nobilis Paulo apostolo inde nato. Cetthim Cithii quorum hodieque civitas Cithium appellatur, Dodanim Rhodii.
